marks.gloss_en: Rav explains his own dictum, 'so that later generations will not laugh at me': the slaughterer wants the slaughter-site soaked with blood so buyers will see it and come
משום צובע אין, משום נטילת נשמה לא? -- [does Rav mean] on account of dyeing yes, on account of taking a life no?
אימא: אף משום צובע -- read Rav as 'also on account of dyeing' (= p_emend_af_tzovea)
say [Rav's dictum as]: ALSO on account of dyeing
the mishna: these are the primary labours -- forty less one
anything that has in it the completion of a labour is liable on account of striking with a hammer
whatever is fit to store and people store its like, and one carried it out on Shabbat -- he is liable to a sin-offering for it
דאי כרבי שמעון, האמר: לא אמרו כל השיעורין הללו אלא למצניעיהן -- for R' Shimon the measures bind only those who store such items, whereas the mishna makes anyone carrying out a storable item liable
R' Yosei bar Chanina: this [clause of the mishna] is not in accordance with R' Shimon
ואידך? -- and the other [Rav Pappa]: is menstrual blood not stored for the cat?
כיון דחלשא לא מצנע ליה -- since it weakens, one does not store it (= p_chalsha_lo_matznia)
Rav Pappa: 'whatever is fit to store' comes to exclude menstrual blood
R' Acha bar Chanina: one who rubs between the pillars on Shabbat is liable on account of smoothing
היינו מולח והיינו מעבד -- salting is tanning, so they are not two labors; R' Yochanan and Reish Lakish concede and replace one with sirtut (p_sirtut_bimkomo)
the mishna lists salting [the hide] among the primary labors
one who wrote one large letter, and there is room in its place to write two, is exempt
